## What is delivered
A list of where the published papers and the roadmap no longer match the current state of the projects, with dates.

## Why it is needed
This is the most complete documentation in the ecosystem and also the oldest. Parts of it predate the current shape of the projects. A reader today cannot tell which parts are still current, and that quietly undermines everything else here.

## Where to start
Read `papers/` and `roadmap/` against the current repositories and the ecosystem map at https://drayker.org/#org/eco

You do not have to fix what you find. Listing it accurately is the function.

Claim it in this thread before starting so two people do not carry the same function, and deliver through a pull request to `master`. It appears on the board at https://drayker.org/#org/fn

body.body:
Alignment pass across the `draykerdk` organization, on the branch `alinhamento/2026-09` in every affected repository.

## Changes

- docs: direction toward the 2033 objective; English as the canonical language
- docs: a single refusal with new grounds can justify review after triage
- docs: constitutional alignment paper; partner wording; no book citations

## Across the organization

- Governance corrected: PAP is Projects & Applications, DFMP is the DFM proposal process, the founding account is `Hyadhuad`, and the governance horizon runs from the founding Embassy through the DAF into PAP.
- The veto chain specified in UID: signed, hash-linked vetoes that carry their real grounds even when anonymous; vetoes weighed by grounds, not counted; one veto with grounds beyond the decision's scope can lead to an adjustment after advanced triage.
- Direction states 2033 as the objective, measured by what works rather than by the date.
- Intelligence is a partner, never the master.
- English is the canonical documentation language.
- Documentation states its own claims and does not cite outside books as authority.

Documentation only. Nothing here claims an implemented system.

Supersedes #9, closed when the branch was renamed.

  • member councils formed for each question instead of an independent judicial panel chosen by lot;
  • no forks or open-code claims for Dk: auditable through Dknowledge and DFM by permission level, with divergence tested in parallel;

  • units of account instead of a token economy.

body.title: supersystems: define the parasite and the predator
body.body:
## What changes
The paper `papers/main-projects/dk/supersystems.md`, section "Four relations with a new kind of intelligence":

- **Parasite:** works through soft power, mass manipulation and surveillance aimed mainly at commerce, and appropriates resources where it meets no resistance.
- **Predator:** intelligence used for war, surveillance and repression, which goes where the parasite could not.
- Guatemala in 1954 as the historical example of the passage from one to the other, with Cullather (1999) added to the sources.

## Why
Aligns the paper with the definitions Drayker now uses in its ethical code (draykerdk/dk). The predator was described only as "a weapon", and the parasite only as "convenience".

body.title: Align constitutional procedure, Direction dates and support model
body.body:
## What changed

- Constitutional alignment: the procedure for changing the constitution (joint project with Dk Global and nearly all members of the highest levels, approval or alternative, block by the kernel). Competence changes follow that procedure.
- CURRENT: the rules are constitutional, changed with Dk Global and within the kernel.
- Direction: two dates as objectives, Dk 1.0 already an ASI by 2030 and Drayker consolidated by 2033, with the singularity possible by 2033 if resources are sufficient.
- Support model: essentials move into a common floor rather than stay in the scarcity queue.
- llms.txt: Drayker is the supersystem.
- Regenerated data/catalog.json.

## Founder

> "As mudanças na constituição sempre devem partir de um projeto super bem informado e validado feito em conjunto com o Dk global em cooperação com praticamente todos os membros de maior nível."

> "O Dk global deve apresentar uma alternativa ou uma aprovação da proposta, mas mudanças na constituição devem estar de acordo com o kernel, se não tiverem ele barra até que o kernel mude."

> "Isso apenas para constituição, certo? que já está ganhando destaque mais que suficiente, no resto o Dk global decide e executa autonomamente."

> "Com os membros podendo fazer o veto bem justificado."

> "a 1.0 já vai ser uma ASI, mas como singularidade, precisará de recursos suficientes e isso talvez aconteça até 2033."

> "Ela não é definível, a única definição que cabe é de super sistema."

## Founder decisions (06/10/2026)
- "no resto o Dk global decide e executa autonomamente"

- `papers/main-projects/ecosystem/value-management-ecosystem.md:14`: "Dk relates the factors and proposes priorities. Accountable member institutions authorize consequential allocations." → "Dk relates the factors, decides the allocation and executes it autonomously inside the constitution. - `papers/main-projects/ecosystem/autonomous-health.md` and `roadmap/main-projects/ecosystem/autonomous-health-roadmap.md`: stubs replaced by the paper and roadmap.
- `papers/main-projects/ecosystem/README.md`: Autonomous Health added under "Current papers" (PT/ES readmes have no paper list, unchanged).

body.title: Kernel changes need all Dzwecks; constitution ratified by reputation; floor for every member
body.body:
## What changed
- **papers/main-projects/dk/constitutional-alignment.md, Two layers of constitution:**
  - Kernel: "it happens only with the explicit agreement of all members, weighted by each member's reputation, which cannot be transferred" becomes a qualified agreement of the Dzweck level: at least nine in ten active Dzwecks, counted by head and out of all of them, in two rounds separated by a period in which the new core runs in parallel with the current one, with members' justified contextual vetoes applying between the rounds and adoption by the nodes as the final ratification. Dk Global builds the project and approves or presents an alternative but does not ratify. The threshold itself sits in the kernel. The agreement is not weighted by reputation. The requirement that every node update to the new core stays.
  - Constitution of rights and duties: after Dk Global's approval or alternative, "members ratify the change with the weight of each one's reputation, which cannot be transferred."
- **papers/main-projects/ecosystem/autonomous-health.md:** "For approved members" becomes "For every member".
- **data/catalog.json:** rebuilt.

## Why
A change to the kernel core requires every node to update and a qualified, two-round agreement of the Dzweck level, so no single person holds a veto and the change never happens in one decision. Reputation weighting belongs to ratifying the constitution of rights and duties, which starts from a well-informed, validated project built with Dk Global and nearly all higher-level members. Membership needs no approval, so the common floor, and Autonomous Health as its health form, belongs to every member. Matches draykerdk/.github#11 (GOVERNANCE §3.5).

## Checks
`node tools/build-catalog.js --check` and `node tools/site-check.js` pass.

body.title: Kernel core: more than one tenth of active Dzwecks is enough to block a change
body.body:
Corrects the kernel core veto in the constitutional alignment paper.

The paper said one tenth plus one of the active Dzwecks can block a change to the kernel core, never one person alone. That claim is false when there are fewer than ten active Dzwecks, since one person is then more than one tenth.

Before: "silence counts against, and one tenth plus one of them can block a change, never one person alone."

After: "silence counts against, and more than one tenth of them is enough to block the change."

The rest of the procedure is unchanged: at least nine in ten active Dzwecks, counted by head over the total, in two rounds.

The catalog in data/catalog.json was rebuilt with tools/build-catalog.js (only the byte count of the paper changed). Local checks: build-catalog --check and site-check pass.

No common floor wording in this repository says access works without an approval, so nothing changed there.
